newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slide on stop-loss selling.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slide on stop-loss selling.

text.p: Argentine bonds slumped Wednesday on stop-loss selling caused by disquiet surrounding a fall in the Mexican peso.
"Stop loss selling set in, sparked by the concerns around the peso," said a trader at a large foreign bank. Trade was average.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slumped $0.40 to 118.15, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1-1/4 to 81-1/2.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional 2 due 2007 fell $0.75 to 101.25.

Attacks on corruption by President Carlos Menem and statements by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo accusing two government ministers of covering up corruption and manipulating judges on Tuesday added to the backdrop of market uncertainty, said traders.
"There is an accumulation of internal and external uncertainty," said another trader.
The first trader said the market would probably continue to slide Thursday "although it is getting nearer to the floor," he added.
Separately, Argentina's industrial production rose by 9.7 percent in September compared to the same month last year, but dropped 3.7 percent from August, the private FIEL consultancy said Thursday.
Output was up 10.1 percent in the third quarter of 1996 compared with the same period last year.
The Economy Ministry said Wednesday the public sector deficit in September was $479 million, compared with $163 million in August.
In the money markets, call money rose to 6.95 percent from 6.75 percent.
